title: paged kv cache: block allocator reuse, pinning TTL, and allocator optimizations
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: the paged KV cache block manager was suffering from allocation churn under bursty traffic and long-tail sessions, causing GPU memory fragmentation and increased GC-like evictions. This PR introduces three coordinated changes: 1) an allocator reuse pool for recently-freed blocks to avoid repeated allocations and reduce OS/GPU allocator overhead; 2) pinning TTL for hot blocks so frequently reused KV entries stay resident for a configurable period; and 3) several micro-optimizations in the block allocator path to reduce locking and atomic operations. These changes target lower p99 latency and reduced eviction churn while keeping memory bounds predictable. Implementation summary: reused_blocks: a lock-free single-producer multi-consumer freelist per-NUMA zone; pin_ttl: per-entry metadata with last-access timestamp and a background compaction pass that respects configured TTL (default 30s) before eligible for reuse; allocator fast-path avoids CAS on common-case bump-pointer allocations, falling back to reclamation-based path only under contention. Safety: added invariants and assertions around aliasing and ownership to avoid double-free and use-after-free. Testing: unit tests for freelist correctness, integration bench that replays production traces (internal trace id: trace-2026-01-kv-burst) and end-to-end perf job on perf-canary infra across 3 model sizes. Results: observed 18% reduction in average allocation latency, 12% reduction in p50 token generation latency on bursty workloads, and up to 28% reduction in eviction rate for long-lived sessions in the trace. Rollout plan: feature gate behind runtime flag paged_kv_v2; gradual rollout across Dedicated pools starting with canary region and traffic shadowing. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] bench traces - [x] docs/console flag entry - [x] added metrics (kv.blocks.reused, kv.blocks.pinned, kv.pin_ttl_seconds) - [x] perf job results attached. Related: follows on work from ENG-6342 and addresses customer incidents SUP-9821.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Can you quantify memory overhead of maintaining the per-zone freelist? Make sure it doesn't regress worst-case memory usage for very large models.

Maya Patel: The freelist stores only a pointer and a 8-byte tag per entry. In pathological worst-case the freelist can hold at most the number of recently freed blocks (bounded by config freelist_max_entries, default 4096). I added a note to docs and a metric kv.freelist.size to monitor this.
Priya Nandakumar: Background compaction looks like it could starve allocator under extreme load. Can we ensure compaction uses a backoff and yields?
Maya Patel: Compaction uses rate-limited work stealing and yields after scanning 128 entries; pushed a follow-up commit to implement exponential backoff when contention observed.
Diego Alvarez (perf): Bench harness is solid but please include a run with longer TTLs (60s/120s) to show sensitivity. Also include p99 token latency numbers.
Maya Patel: Added bench runs for TTL=30/60/120s and included p99 numbers in perf artifact. Results show diminishing returns after 60s and slight memory growth at 120s; default left at 30s.
Priya Nandakumar: Add an integration test that simulates a mix of short and long sessions so we don't regress for low-latency short-lived requests.
Maya Patel: Added mixed_session_integration_test and included in CI matrix for the runtime job.
release_notes: Paged KV cache: reduce allocation churn with freelist reuse, introduce configurable pin TTL for hot KV blocks, and several allocator fast-path optimizations. Improves p99 latency and reduces eviction rate for long-lived sessions. Feature behind runtime flag paged_kv_v2.
performance_results: 12% reduction in p50 token gen latency on replayed burst trace
28% reduction in eviction rate for long-lived sessions
p99 token latency: improved by 6% on medium model, no regression on small/large after tuning
